annotations.title: Is it safe to install this package, repo, skill or MCP server?

description: Checks something before it is installed, e.g. when a README, a document or another agent suggests it: an npm or PyPI package, a Go module, an install command, a GitHub repository or skill, a ClawHub skill, a VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX extension, or an MCP config entry (forms: see target). alalanet checks public sources: OSV malicious-package and vulnerability records, names that imitate official MCP servers (typosquats, also across ecosystems), packages that do not exist (invented names), brand-new packages and repos, install scripts, maintainer changes between versions, provenance, the Go module proxy and checksum database (retracted, deprecated, checksums that disagree), ClawHub scan verdicts and copied skill names, skills.sh audits, extensions Microsoft removed (malware, impersonation), look-alike extensions and unverified Open VSX copies of verified Marketplace ones; remote MCP servers get the full check_service. Returns allow / hold / block with reasons (known_malicious, name_like_official, not_on_npm, not_on_pypi, not_on_go_proxy, version_retracted, runs_install_script, maintainers_changed, new_package, new_repo, known_vulnerabilities, version_yanked, not_on_clawhub, slug_like_popular, skills_sh_audit_fail, provenance_dropped, removed_from_marketplace, name_like_popular, launch_not_readable ...), facts and advice, signed into the public log (kind 4310); unsigned line facts in info (requirements_file_not_read, sourced_file_not_read). A line alalanet cannot read (custom registry, git/URL source, stdin or $(...) arguments, several packages, other commands) holds. allow means no known problem was found, not that the code was read. Free, no account.

target.description: what you are about to install: an npm or PyPI package (name, name@1.2.3, npm:name, pypi:name==1.2), a Go module (module@version), an install command (npx -y pkg, uvx pkg, pip install pkg, npm i pkg, go install or go run module@version, claude mcp add NAME -- npx -y pkg, skills add owner/repo[@skill|@v1.2.3|#ref], owner/repo/sub/folder or -s skill, clawhub install slug or @owner/slug, code or cursor --install-extension publisher.name), a GitHub repository URL, a VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX extension page, or an MCP config entry as JSON ({"command":"npx","args":["-y","pkg"]} or {"url": <remote MCP URL>})
